subject.title: [Feature]: Make agent-generated setup commands aware of the user's login shell

question: Should OpenClaw standardize agent-generated local setup snippets on explicit interpreter wrapping by default, with shell-native rendering only for a small supported set of detected or user-confirmed shells?
rationale: Both approaches can prevent the reported failure, but they differ in portability, prompt complexity, cross-platform support, and how much host metadata should enter agent context.

options.title: Use explicit interpreter targeting
options.body: Require shell-specific setup snippets to state and invoke Bash or POSIX sh explicitly unless the user has selected a supported shell.

options.title: Add supported shell rendering
options.body: Expose validated login-shell metadata and render native Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell snippets where supported.

options.title: Ask before shell-specific commands
options.body: Have the agent ask for the user's target shell whenever it cannot safely provide interpreter-neutral guidance.

recommendation.title: Use explicit interpreter targeting
recommendation.body: Require shell-specific setup snippets to state and invoke Bash or POSIX sh explicitly unless the user has selected a supported shell.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing login-shell and gateway execution boundary has substantial recent ownership from this contributor.
